LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 5.3.1 WORD CLASS: REGULAR AND IRREGULAR ADJECTIVES

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.3: Grammar in use 5.3.1 Word Class: Regular and Irregular Adjectives
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grammar in use 5.3.1 Word Class: Regular and Irregular Adjectives, part of Strand 5 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four General.

Key inquiry question: Why should we say the correct shape and size of things? How do you use words to talk about how someone feels or looks? 2. How do we describe things?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Grammar in use 5.3.1 Word Class: Regular and Irregular Adjectives together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: learner uses adjectives correctly in sentence as they interact with peers.

● Self-efficacy: learner confidently uses adjectives correctly in their day-to-day communication.

Values:
● Unity: is promoted the learners cohesively relate with each to perform activities such as identifying and discussing adjectives.

● Responsibility: is cultivated as the learner takes personal initiative to complete assigned roles.

Link to other subjects:

The learner is able to connect the concept of comparative adjectives to the learning in English and Kiswahili.
